chunks: When God alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter are filled with resentment. And when those [other than God] are mentioned, they begin to rejoice.

key_terms.اشْمَأَزَّتْ: were filled with resentment or displeasure
key_terms.الْآخِرَةِ: the Hereafter / the life to come

ai.seo_question: Why do disbelievers feel resentment when God is mentioned but rejoice when idols are mentioned?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (often linked with 39:17) illustrates the spiritual pathology of the *kuffar*, whose hearts recoil from the majesty of Allah due to their attachment to worldly idols (*awthan*). The contrast between their inward 'shrinking' (*ishma'azzat*) and outward 'rejoicing' (*yastabshirun*) reveals a dissonance where false deities provide immediate, albeit superficial, comfort, while the Divine presence demands a deeper, often resisted, spiritual awakening.
